To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) IT PMs believe that the most important skill categories are client management, communication and problem solving, (ii) the skill categories are combined to form four distinct archetypes, and (iii) the four archetypes are: General Manager, Problem Solving Manager, Client Representative and Balances Manager.

IT project managers exhibit a set of skills that fall into nine skill categories, that the skills are combined in four different archetypes, and that the archetypes differ in the relative importance of the skills.
IT PMs construct four archetypes of successful IT PMs, and these archetypes are characterized by different combinations of nine skill categories.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question, “what skills do successful IT PMs possess?”.
the question: What skills do IT project managers use to manage IT projects?
the question of what constitutes effective project management practice in the IT sector.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the study provides an understanding of what successful IT PMs do and how they do it.
the IT project managers' construction is that of a general manager with a strong emphasis on problem solving, communication, planning, control and client management skills.

IT project management is a complex process, requiring a wide range of skills and abilities, which must be applied in a balanced manner, depending on the specific circumstances and context in which the project is being undertaken.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IT PM skills can be categorized into nine distinct skill categories and can be further classified into four archetypes.
we have identified a set of skills and archetypes that can serve as a basis for future research and practice in the area of IT PM.
IT project managers' construction and use of successful IT project management practice is a complex and dynamic process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IT PMs should be encouraged to develop a broad range of skills, and to tailor their skill sets to the needs of the projects they are managing.
there is no single best way to be a successful IT PM.
IT PM skills are complex, and that IT PMs should not be expected to be equally skilled at each of the nine skill categories.
